A wide saddle of moss packed into the crotch where three great boughs divide fills the near picture, the massive trunk rising out of the top of the frame behind it, the moss a thumb-deep mat threaded with copper rootlets and studded with lichen rosettes the size of a fingernail, a thin band of canopy far below, a single amber snail crossing the whole mossy floor mid-route.

A bracket fungus shelf juts from the trunk filling the left side of the picture and rising out of the top, the bracket's upper surface close underfoot and pored with cream-and-rust concentric rings, beaded along its far rim with cold dew, grit and pine needles pressed into the soft outer edge, a thin band of treetops below.

A shelf of exposed root where the bank has washed out fills the near picture, the bank itself climbing out of frame behind, the roots plaited into a floor of arm-thick coils packed with grit and dropped leaves, a loop of grass cord tied to one root at the lip as a handhold, a thin band of fern below.

A wide horizontal bough with a saddle of moss worn flat in the middle fills the near picture, the trunk going up out of the top of the frame behind it, bark plated like old armour and a rain-pool cupped in a hollow at the near edge, the bough running out of frame left and right, a thin band of canopy below.

The broad top of a mushroom cap seen only as its own surface underfoot fills the near picture, the cap running out of frame on three sides with the stalk out of sight below, the skin faintly ribbed and waxy, one gill-ridge showing at the cropped near edge beaded with cold dew, a moth resting open-winged at the far margin, a thin band of treetops beyond.

A split in a lightning-opened trunk fills the near picture, its two scorched walls rising out of frame above on either side, the split floor littered with charcoal crumbs and a mat of pale lichen colonising the inner wood, a peg of hazel driven into the crack at the lip serving as a handhold, a thin band of leaves far below.

A knot of high roots where an old beech overhangs a gully fills the near picture, the trunk going up out of the top of the frame, the roots woven into a cradle of pale-grey rope-wood packed between with grit and one crushed acorn cup, a thin band of gully ferns below, one root glistening where resin has bled through the bark.

A mossy step in a root buttress fills the near picture, the buttress climbing out of frame above and the great trunk filling the left side, the step's surface a dense pad of star-moss in violent emerald, each tiny star distinct at arm's reach, three flat river pebbles set as footing near the edge, a thin band of forest floor below.

A broad burl swelling from a trunk fills the near picture like a stepping stone, the trunk filling the left side and rising out of the top of the frame, the burl's top a whorl of knotted grain worn smooth, flecked with old lichen and one split seam crusted with amber resin, three flat stones set as a step at the base, a thin band of moonlit leaves below.

A hollow worn in the flank of a fallen giant fills the near picture, the trunk running out of frame both ways so only this stretch shows, the wood inside soft and fibrous and furred with violet-tinged moss, the rim scalloped smooth by decades of rain, a loop of bark-cord tied to a root spur at the lip, a thin band of ferns far below.

A wide fork where an oak limb splits fills the near picture, the great trunk going up out of the top of the frame behind it, bark furrows deep enough to put a hand in, a saddle of moss worn flat in the middle and bark scales lifting at the edges, both branches running out of frame left and right, a thin band of misted treetops below.

A landing where a stair of exposed roots levels out fills the near picture, the bank climbing out of frame behind and the root stair dropping out of frame below, the landing packed with grit and dropped needles and a fur of copper moss, a bark wedge propped against the upper root as a step, a thin band of forest floor below, a violet beetle paused mid-crossing.

A shelf of loose bark lifting from a dead standing pine fills the near picture, the trunk going up out of the top of the frame and the lifted bark curving up like a lip at the far side, the bark surface dusty with red rot and punky at one corner, a twig peg driven in near the edge, a thin band of dead bracken below.

A natural arch of root with the far end running out of frame fills the near picture, the root rising from the bank that climbs out of frame behind, the arch's flat top gritty with old soil and lichen and one fresh split gleaming pale where the bark has cracked, a thin band of stream below, a single droplet hanging from the arch's underside.

A wide branch-junction deep inside the canopy fills the near picture, leaves closing over one full side of the frame and the trunk going up out of the top, the junction floored with wind-gathered leaf mould and a pad of foam-green moss, bark ridges raised like roof-ribs underfoot, a bundle of spare twigs lashed to a side spur, a thin band of lower canopy below.

A mossy step on the upper side of a root buttress where it levels into a platform fills the near picture, the buttress rising out of the top of the frame and the trunk filling the right side, the step's surface a tightly packed cushion of rounded moss heads each the size of a pea, glistening, a thin band of woodland below, a dewdrop gone milky with cold on one moss head.

A crotch where two great hornbeam limbs divide fills the near picture, the trunk going up out of the top of the frame and the limbs running out of frame on either side, the floor of the crotch packed with rotted heartwood and a mat of pale lichen, bark lips raised on either side like a cradle wall, a thin band of field below, one loose bead resting against a bark lip.

A long burl running along the side of a beech trunk fills the near picture like a bench, the trunk filling the right side and going out of the top of the frame, the burl's upper face a ripple of raised grain smooth as old leather and patched with flat lichen, one knot hole plugged with dead moss, a thin band of roots and leaf litter below.

A wide fork where a beech limb splits fills the near picture, the great trunk going up out of the top behind it, bark smooth as river-clay and silver-grey, the saddle between the arms worn flat and packed with two seasons of mast and dropped lichen, both limbs running out of frame left and right, a thin band of canopy below — one amber-bodied beetle has wedged itself under a loose curl of bark at the fork's heart and gone still.

A bracket fungus shelf swelling from a trunk fills the near picture, the trunk rising out of the top and filling the whole right side, the bracket's upper surface ridged in tight concentric waves the colour of old honey, each ridge holding a line of cold dew, the near edge showing a thin fringe of buff pores, a thin band of understorey far below — a moth rests at the bracket's uphill corner, wings pressed flat, the eyespots staring up.

A mossy step in a root buttress fills the near picture, the great ash trunk climbing out of the top behind it and the buttress wall running out of frame both sides, the step's surface a dense mat of star-moss in deep emerald packed with dropped seeds and one flat river pebble left from a previous night, a thin band of leaf-litter and fern far below — a single acorn cap sits upright on the pebble, filled to its rim with last night's rain.

A hollow worn into the flank of a fallen giant fills the near picture, the trunk running out of frame left and right so only this crescent of it shows, the wood inside fibrous and rust-red and furred with turquoise lichen in rosettes the size of a fingernail, a thin crust of frost along the hollow's lower lip, a thin band of bracken far below — a pill-bug has curled into a perfect sphere in the hollow's deepest corner and caught the light.

A long burl running along a beech trunk like a bench fills the near picture, the trunk rising out of the top and running out of both sides, its surface a swirling grain of amber and copper polished to a dull gleam, furred at the edges with lichen in rosettes the size of a thumbnail, one split in the wood holding a puddle of collected rain gone faintly green; a thin band of canopy far below, open sky above.

The crotch where three great ash branches meet fills the near picture, the branches running out of frame in three directions, the trunk dropping out of sight below, the floor between them packed with decades of bark flake and composted leaf pressed into a springy mat, a loop of moss-cord tied around one branch as a handhold at the outer edge, a fat amber snail crossing the whole mat on a diagonal leaving a glittering trail; a thin band of treetops far below, open sky above.

A broad crotch where three beech limbs diverge fills the near picture, the great trunk rising out of the top behind them and the limbs running out of frame on three sides, the bark smooth and pearl-grey with wrinkles bunching at each joint, a colony of lichen in flat rosettes the size of a thumbnail pressed into every crease, the moss in the saddle worn to a shine in one oval patch, a single acorn cap wedged upright in a fold of bark as if left there on purpose, one thin band of canopy below, open sky above.
